title: Infimum of an extended-natural family bounded by a coercion
statement: Let $(f_i)_{i \in \iota}$ be a family of values in the extended natural numbers $\bbn_\infty = \bbn \cup \{\infty\}$, indexed by an arbitrary type $\iota$, and let $n \in \bbn$. Then $\inf_{i} f_i \le n$ if and only if there exists an index $i$ with $f_i \le n$, where $n$ is regarded as an element of $\bbn_\infty$ via the canonical inclusion.
hypotheses_covered: family of extended-natural values indexed by an arbitrary type
a natural number n coerced into the extended naturals
replaced:
Let $\iota$ be a type and $f : \iota \to \mathbb{N}_\infty$ an $\mathbb{N}_\infty$-valued
family.  Then $\inf_{i} f(i) \le n$ if and only if there exists an index $i$ such that
$f(i) \le n$.  Here $n : \mathbb{N}$ is coerced into $\mathbb{N}_\infty = \mathrm{ENat}$.
